rationale: A coherent and internally consistent swap of the collateral leg from act/at to che/lct inside the archive's best composite, motivated by the cash-purity decomposition, but it remains a one-component substitution within an already well-mined family and the che/lct leg previously showed near-zero cross-sectional slope, so expect alpha gain without much fmb improvement.

target_name: Excess Market Distress With Servicing Capacity
rationale: Promoting the distress-gap from standalone valuation measure to the scaled leg is a genuine structural change with a clear economic story and consistent sign logic; the main caveat is that lt appears in both legs, so part of any result may be mechanical rather than a market-versus-fundamentals disagreement effect.

The near-identical revt/act version already produced a reliably negative alpha (t = -4.15), so a positive expected sign is asserted against the archive's own evidence, and stripping cash from the denominator largely re-imports the separately documented cash-purity effect, confounding the very diagnostic the proposal claims to run.

Combining the cash stock and the operating cash flow into a single horizon-matched coverage ratio against current liabilities is dimensionally sound, economically well-motivated as a lender's renewal test, and structurally distinct from the archive's rank-blend and act-based liquidity constructs.

A single-operator robustness check rather than a new mechanism, and therefore low on novelty, but the industry-determined nature of balance-sheet composition ratios makes this a legitimately informative falsification test of the archive's central claim.

This is an average of two already-tested valuation anchors against an unchanged survival leg — both parent signals scored alpha t-stats of 3.2–3.8 — so the result is near-certain to interpolate between them and constitutes a cosmetic consolidation rather than a new economic hypothesis.
